name: Tobramycin
route_note: IV/IM with level monitoring; nebulised solution or dry-powder inhaler for cystic fibrosis; eye drops and ointment.
targets: 16S rRNA of the 30S ribosomal subunit (A site)

discovery.note: A component of the nebramycin complex produced by Streptomyces tenebrarius. Year Lilly described the nebramycin complex from which tobramycin was isolated; Wikipedia gives 1965 as the patent year.

tagline: Aminoglycoside favoured for Pseudomonas, notably inhaled in cystic fibrosis
summary: Tobramycin is an aminoglycoside from Streptomyces tenebrarius with slightly greater intrinsic activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa than gentamicin. Inhaled tobramycin is a standard suppressive therapy for chronic Pseudomonas infection in cystic fibrosis, and eye drops are widely used for bacterial conjunctivitis.
mechanism: Aminoglycosides are polycationic molecules that cross the Gram-negative outer membrane by self-promoted uptake and enter the cytoplasm by an oxygen-dependent transport process, which is why they are inactive against anaerobes. Inside, they bind the decoding A site of 16S rRNA in the 30S subunit, causing misreading of mRNA and production of aberrant proteins that damage the membrane, accelerating uptake; killing is rapid and concentration-dependent.
Inhaled formulations deliver very high airway concentrations that exceed MICs of most P. aeruginosa isolates while keeping systemic exposure low.
uses: Chronic Pseudomonas aeruginosa lung infection in cystic fibrosis (inhaled)
Serious Gram-negative infections including Pseudomonas (IV, usually with a beta-lactam)
Bacterial conjunctivitis and other external eye infections (ophthalmic)
Combined with dexamethasone in eye drops for inflammatory eye conditions with infection risk

history.title: Gentamicin precedent
history.detail: Gentamicin is discovered at Schering, establishing aminoglycosides as anti-pseudomonal agents.

history.title: Nebramycin complex
history.detail: Lilly scientists describe the nebramycin complex from Streptomyces tenebrarius, from which tobramycin was isolated.

history.title: Clinical introduction
history.detail: Injectable tobramycin (Nebcin) enters US clinical use in the mid-1970s.

history.title: TOBI
history.detail: The FDA approves preservative-free tobramycin inhalation solution (TOBI) for cystic fibrosis, based on trials showing improved lung function.

history.title: Bethkis
history.detail: A further tobramycin inhalation solution (Bethkis) is approved in the US for cystic fibrosis.

pk.bioavailability: negligible orally; low systemic absorption after inhalation

safety.boxed_warning: Parenteral labels warn of nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity and neurotoxicity with potential for neuromuscular blockade; inhaled and ophthalmic products do not carry this boxed warning.

facts: Tobramycin eye drops (Tobrex) and tobramycin-dexamethasone (Tobradex) are among the most prescribed ophthalmic antibiotics.
